title: Pandas Data Analysis — Student Marks Dataset
description: Load, clean, analyze, and visualize a student marks dataset using Pandas and Matplotlib
objective: Students will create a CSV dataset, load it with Pandas, perform groupby aggregations, and generate 3 charts — practicing the complete data analysis workflow

steps.title: Create the Dataset
steps.instructions:
Create a file called `students.csv` with this data (at least 20 rows):

```csv
name,roll,course,hindi,english,maths,science,computer,city
Rahul Sharma,101,ADCA,78,82,70,75,88,Bhopal
Priya Patel,102,DCA,85,90,88,82,95,Indore
Amit Kumar,103,ADCA,45,50,35,40,60,Delhi
Sneha Gupta,104,ADCA,92,88,85,90,94,Bhopal
Vikram Singh,105,DCA,38,42,30,35,45,Jaipur
```

Add at least 15 more students with varied marks, courses, and cities.

Now create `analysis.py`:
```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_csv("students.csv")
print(f"Loaded {len(df)} students")
print(df.head())
print(df.info())
```

Run: `python analysis.py` — verify the data loads correctly.

steps.title: Calculate Results and Explore
steps.instructions:
Add calculated columns:
```python
subjects = ["hindi", "english", "maths", "science", "computer"]
df["total"] = df[subjects].sum(axis=1)
df["percentage"] = (df["total"] / 500) * 100
df["grade"] = df["percentage"].apply(
    lambda p: "A+" if p >= 90 else "A" if p >= 75 else "B" if p >= 60 else "C" if p >= 45 else "F"
)
```

Explore the data:
```python
# Basic statistics
print(df["percentage"].describe())

# Top 5 students
print(df.nlargest(5, "percentage")[["name", "course", "percentage", "grade"]])

# Students who failed any subject (below 33)
for sub in subjects:
    failed = df[df[sub] < 33]
    if len(failed) > 0:
        print(f"\nFailed in {sub}: {list(failed['name'])}")

# Course-wise average
print(df.groupby("course")["percentage"].mean())

# City-wise count
print(df["city"].value_counts())
```

Read each output and understand what it tells you.

steps.title: Create Charts
steps.instructions:
Chart 1 — Subject averages (bar chart):
```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
avgs = df[subjects].mean()
avgs.plot(kind="bar", ax=ax, color=["#ef4444", "#f59e0b", "#3b82f6", "#10b981", "#6366f1"])
ax.set_title("Average Marks by Subject")
ax.set_ylabel("Average Marks")
ax.set_xticklabels([s.capitalize() for s in subjects], rotation=0)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("chart_subjects.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
```

Chart 2 — Grade distribution (pie chart):
```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6))
df["grade"].value_counts().plot(kind="pie", ax=ax, autopct="%1.0f%%")
ax.set_title("Grade Distribution")
ax.set_ylabel("")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("chart_grades.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
```

Chart 3 — Course-wise box plot:
```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
df.boxplot(column="percentage", by="course", ax=ax)
ax.set_title("Marks Distribution by Course")
ax.set_ylabel("Percentage")
plt.suptitle("")  # remove auto-title
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("chart_boxplot.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
```

steps.title: Generate a Summary Report
steps.instructions:
Add a summary at the end:
```python
print("\n" + "=" * 50)
print("  ANALYSIS SUMMARY")
print("=" * 50)
print(f"Total Students: {len(df)}")
print(f"Pass Rate: {len(df[df['percentage'] >= 33]) / len(df) * 100:.0f}%")
print(f"Class Average: {df['percentage'].mean():.1f}%")
print(f"Topper: {df.loc[df['percentage'].idxmax(), 'name']} ({df['percentage'].max():.1f}%)")
print(f"\nGrade Breakdown:")
for grade, count in df['grade'].value_counts().items():
    print(f"  {grade}: {count} students")

print(f"\nCharts saved: chart_subjects.png, chart_grades.png, chart_boxplot.png")
```

Verify:
- All 3 charts are saved as PNG files
- Charts have proper titles and labels
- Summary numbers match your data

steps.title: Export Results to Excel
steps.instructions:
Save the full results to an Excel file:
```python
# Add grade to each student and save
df_result = df[["name", "roll", "course", "total", "percentage", "grade", "city"]].copy()
df_result = df_result.sort_values("percentage", ascending=False)
df_result.to_excel("student_results.xlsx", index=False)
print("Saved: student_results.xlsx")

# Also create a course-wise summary sheet
with pd.ExcelWriter("full_report.xlsx") as writer:
    df_result.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="All Students", index=False)
    course_summary = df.groupby("course").agg(
        students=("name", "count"),
        avg_pct=("percentage", "mean"),
        pass_rate=("percentage", lambda x: (x >= 33).sum() / len(x) * 100),
    ).round(1)
    course_summary.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Course Summary")
print("Saved: full_report.xlsx (2 sheets)")
```

(Install openpyxl if needed: `pip install openpyxl`)

Open `full_report.xlsx` in Excel — verify both sheets have correct data.

**Submit:** Your `analysis.py`, `students.csv`, 3 chart PNG files, and `full_report.xlsx`.
